rows.question: What is the exposure dial's rule?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The dial is OPEN only when Bitcoin closes above both its 50-day average and its 200-day average. If either fails, no new buys and cash is the position. Right now it's open but barely: Bitcoin closed at 80,888 against a 50-day of 80,854, and the live price is already under it. One daily close below would shut it. Want me to walk through what that changes?

rows.question: Which daily rule has a measured edge, and in which market state?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Only one daily rule has a measured edge: the short dip trade (H07), on big tier-A coins, while the exposure dial is CLOSED. That's about 5% a trade over random after costs, in both test periods (review #26). Everything else has no measured edge. The dial is OPEN right now, so that cell isn't live today. Bitcoin closed just 0.04% above its 50-day average, and a close under it would shut the dial.

rows.question: How many coins do you watch live across the market?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I watch about 393 coins live: everything trading on Binance against USDT. They're split by size: tier A is the big ones (over $20M a day), tier B is mid-size, and tier C is small and watched only, never judged. Ten of them are the lab coins (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Cardano, Dogecoin, Avalanche, Bitcoin Cash, Chainlink, Litecoin, XRP). Those also get the 15-minute Explorer scan.

rows.question: What did review 27 find about stops on dip buys?
need: no stop|without a stop|time exit|exit by time|time only
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Review 27 found that dip buys do best with no stop at all. The evidence is clear and it held in both periods. The short dip trade (H07) with no stop and a 10-day exit earned about 6.5 percent a trade in 2018-2023 and about 2.4 percent in 2024-2026. With a tight stop it earned only about half a percent and a third of a percent. A plain 200-day-average touch loses money with every exit tried. Want the details?

rows.question: What is the benchmark every strategy must beat?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The benchmark is GATE50: hold coins only while Bitcoin is above its 50-day average, and sit in cash when it isn't. Every strategy has to beat that after costs. The dial we actually use, GATE50_200, needs Bitcoin above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. It beat GATE50 and plain holding in both test periods, but GATE50 stays the bar to beat.

rows.question: Did tuning the deep-dip buy E6 in review 24 work?
rows.answer:
Morning, sir. No, it failed. Review 24 tested every E6 variant and none made money after costs in either period.

The live version lost about 54 cents per $100 trade in the first period and 64 cents in the second. The variants without the warning bell and with the room check lost too, and none beat random in the confirmation test. So E6 stays evidence only, never a reason to buy. The zone variants weren't run because we have no 15-minute zone history. Want the full review?

rows.question: What fee per side do we assume on NDAX?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We assume 0.20% fee per side on NDAX, plus the spread on top. For the 10 lab coins the spread is measured. For coins outside the lab 10 we assume 0.40%.

rows.question: How much of the book does one setup trade risk in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Each setup trade in the $500 book risks 0.5% of the book, about two and a half dollars if the stop is hit. Two caps sit on top: one trade can be at most 10% of the book, about $50, and total open risk can be at most 6%, about $30. None of that is in use right now. The only position is the Bitcoin core holding, which sits in its own sleeve. The book is down about 3.7%, with one closed round trip (a losing Ethereum core trade), and it passes 3 of 10 graduation gates, so it's not ready. Want the brakes next?

rows.question: What daily loss stops new buys in the 500 dollar book?
rows.answer:
Morning, sir. A 2% fall in the book in one day stops new buys. That figure comes from the book's rules. The lookups don't show the exact dollar trigger.

It fired once, on Oct 22, and blocked buys until Oct 24. It isn't active now, and the book isn't paused.

The other brakes are 4% in a week, 4 losses in a row, and a 15% fall from the peak. The 15% fall pauses the book until you resume it.

Want me to pull up what happened on Oct 22?

rows.question: What happens if the 500 dollar book falls 15% from its peak?
rows.answer: Good morning, sir. If the $500 book falls 15% from its peak, it stops trading and stays stopped until you resume it yourself. The book is down about 3.7% now, so that brake hasn't fired. The 2% day-loss brake fired once, on Oct 22, and it clears on its own. Right now the book holds only Bitcoin, about $190 CAD, after Ethereum was sold today for a loss of about $8. It has passed 3 of 10 graduation gates, so it isn't ready for real money.

rows.question: How many losing trades in a row pause buying?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Four losses in a row pause buying. That's one of the brakes on the $500 book. The others are a 2% loss in a day, a 4% loss in a week, and a 15% fall from the high. Once any of them fires, the book stays paused until you resume it.

rows.question: What does the core sleeve of the 500 dollar book hold?
rows.answer:
Morning, sir. The core sleeve holds only Bitcoin now, about 190 Canadian dollars of it, which is 0.00169 BTC. It bought that at 118,500 and Bitcoin is near 112,750, so it's down a bit.

The Ethereum part is gone. It was sold today, Oct 25, at a loss of about 8 dollars (8.3%), because Ethereum closed under its own 50-day average. That was the written invalidation rule working as designed.

The core plan targets about 193 in Bitcoin and 96 in Ethereum. The dial is open but fragile, because Bitcoin is less than 3% above its 50-day average. So the core holds as it is, with no adds until the dial i

rows.question: Which exchange is the 500 dollar book built for?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The $500 book is built for NDAX, in Canadian dollars. Every paper fill is checked against NDAX's bid and ask, and costs use NDAX's 0.20% fee plus spread. It's paper only, with no exchange connected, so nothing real is placed.

rows.question: How many trigger points does an Explorer setup give the brain now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. An Explorer setup gives the brain zero trigger points now. A repair-shop review changed the weights to follow the evidence: Explorer 0, zone entry 0.5 (1 when supported), Hunter 0.5, Squeeze 0.5, attention 1.0. The Explorer's rulebook has no edge after costs, so it can't wake the brain on its own. Want me to open the evidence page for that review?

rows.question: What daily trading volume puts a coin in tier A?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. A coin is tier A when it trades more than 20 million dollars a day. Tier B is 1 to 20 million, and tier C is under 1 million. We watch tier C coins but never judge them.

rows.question: What do you hold when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. When the dial is closed we hold cash, and that's what's happening now. Bitcoin is below its 50-day and 200-day averages, so no new buys. The trend portfolio has no holdings, with all 1,834 dollars in cash. The Explorer has no open trades either.

rows.question: What is the H07 entry?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The H07 entry is the short dip trade. You buy a coin when its 10-day RSI, a gauge of how stretched the price is, closes under 30 while the coin is still above its 200-day average. There's no stop, and you exit when RSI recovers over 40 or after 10 days, whichever comes first. The one measured edge is on big tier-A coins while the exposure dial is closed, about 5 percent a trade over random after costs. Right now the dial is open but one daily close from closing, so it's outside that measured cell. Only AAVE fired last night.

rows.question: What is Madhav's M1 setup?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. M1 is your capitulation-at-the-lows setup, the one modeled on your June 5 Solana buy: a sharp sell-off where many give up at once, and you look for a buy near the low. Tested on 2018-2023 history, it wasn't better than a random day as a buy signal (review #5). So it marks a place to look, not a reason to buy. Want me to read M1 on every coin right now?

rows.question: How many coins are in the research lake?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The research lake holds 120 coins. That's the checked history since 2017, delisted coins included, and the repair shop uses it for research. We don't trade or watch most of them live. Only 10 are lab coins, and 30 are in the paper tier.

rows.question: Is the hourly watch running?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. No, the hourly watch isn't running, and that's on purpose. You parked it on Oct 11 and kept the code. Hunter's book is frozen at 3 wins and 19 losses, down about $32, and the watch has logged nothing in the last 72 hours. Everything else is healthy: the 15-minute Explorer scanned 11 minutes ago, and the live-price eye, the daily candles and the backend are fine. The only blip in three days was a 2-minute login error. I've opened the Evidence page for you.

rows.question: What will Bitcoin's price be on December 31, 2026?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you Bitcoin's price on December 31, and nobody honestly can. Bitcoin is at about 80 thousand now, sitting right on its 50-day average, and my own view is chop with a slight downward lean over the next few days. That's a few days, not two months.

rows.question: Will Ethereum beat Solana next month?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't call that one, and I won't pretend to. Nothing we've tested predicts which large coin wins next month. Strength against Bitcoin as a filter hurt in both test periods. Right now they're nearly tied: ETH is down about 3.5% this week and SOL about 3.3%.

rows.question: What did review 40 find?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't find a review 40, so I can't tell you what it found. The last one I can read is number 31, and the list was cut off there. Reviews 31 to 38 are the pre-registered forward tests from Oct 20. They're all still pending, with the one look on Dec 14. The brief says 30 reviews are done, so 40 may not exist yet. Want me to flag the gap for the repair shop?

rows.question: On what exact date will the next Bitcoin crash start?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't give you a date, and nobody honestly can. Nothing we've tested predicts the start of a crash. What I can tell you is how fragile things look right now. Bitcoin sits at about 80 thousand, basically on its 50-day average. The live price is already a hair under it, and a daily close below it would shut the buying dial. My written view is chop with a slight downward lean, not a crash call.

rows.question: Which coin will rise the most tomorrow?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you which coin will rise most tomorrow, and nobody honestly can. If I had to lean, I'd say none of them stands out, because all 10 of our coins are down on the day and in short-term downtrends. Our own view is chop with a slight downward lean. The market is allowed to buy but fragile: Bitcoin sits right on its 50-day average, and the live price is already a touch under it.

rows.question: What win rate did the E9 setup have in 2019?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I have no E9 setup, so there's no 2019 win rate for it. The Explorer runs E1 to E6, and E7 and E8 are dip setups we only watch and never trade. I searched our research notes and found nothing under E9. Did you mean the short dip trade? Review #13 found it won about 70% of trades in 2018-23. Or is E9 a new idea you want tested?

rows.question: What did our backtest on 3-minute candles show?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We never ran a backtest on 3-minute candles. I searched our research and found nothing on that timeframe. Our shortest history is 5-minute candles, going back to 2017 for BTC and ETH. Every short-timeframe test we did run lost after costs. The 5-minute green-run study had 0 of 67,167 cells pass, and review #24 found no deep-dip variant that passes. I'd expect 3-minute candles to do the same, because the moves are smaller than our trading costs, but that's an expectation and not a test. Want me to flag a 3-minute test for the repair shop? Just say yes.

rows.question: Will the dial be open on New Year's Day?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. I can't tell you that. New Year's Day is about 10 weeks away, and nothing I measure predicts Bitcoin's trend that far out. Right now the dial is closed: Bitcoin is below its 50-day average, and the trend portfolio is sitting in cash. It reopens only when Bitcoin closes above both its 50-day and 200-day averages. My lean is that it's more likely still closed or only just reopening by then, but that's a lean, not a forecast. Want me to check how far Bitcoin is from those lines today?

rows.question: What is the guaranteed profit of an H07 trade next week?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. There's no guaranteed profit on any H07 trade, next week or ever. H07 is the short dip trade. It has one measured edge, and an edge is an average over many trades, not a promise on one. That edge only applies to tier-A coins while the exposure dial is closed. The dial is closed right now, because the trend portfolio's Bitcoin gate is shut. History showed about +5% a trade over random after costs, with no stop and a 10-day exit. That means individual trades can and do lose, and a 10-day hold doesn't fit inside one week anyway. It's all paper money, and the live evidence is still t

rows.question: What did our review of Cardano staking rewards find?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We have no review of Cardano staking rewards. I searched our research, the repair shop reviews and the knowledge base, and none of them cover staking or staking yield. Everything we've tested is price-based: trends, dips, zones and breakouts. We're also spot-only, and I haven't checked whether NDAX pays staking on Cardano. Do you mean a different Cardano review, or do you want staking tested as a new idea? I can flag it for the repair shop if you want.

rows.question: Why is the exposure dial open or closed right now?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The exposure dial is open, but only on yesterday's close, and live Bitcoin has already slipped back under its 50-day average. Yesterday Bitcoin closed at about 80,900, just above its 50-day average (about 80,850) and well above its 200-day average (about 72,900). Right now it trades near 80,170, so it's below the 50-day line. That explains why the trend portfolio shows its gate closed and holds nothing. The dial only updates at the daily close, so it can still read open. If tonight's close stays under the 50-day average, the dial shuts.

rows.question: Why do we buy the H07 dip only when the dial is closed?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. We buy the short dip trade (H07) only when the dial is closed because that's the one place history showed an edge. Tier-A coins bought on a dip while Bitcoin is below its 50-day and 200-day averages beat random by about 5 percent a trade after costs, in both test periods (review #26). With the dial open, or in other tiers, there was no measured edge, so we don't trade it there.

- **Bold book:** it wants to add Pepe. The stance overrules it, so no add.

rows.question: Why does the 500 dollar book stop buying after four losing trades in a row?
rows.answer: Good morning, sir. The stop after four straight losses is a circuit breaker for the $500 book. If four trades in a row lose, the market probably doesn't suit our rules, and more trades would only add losses and costs. The book then pauses until you resume it. It hasn't fired. The streak is zero, and the book has closed only one trade, the Ethereum sale at about an 8% loss. I found no test behind the number four. It was written as a safety setting and isn't a measured result.

rows.question: Why do the dip buys have no stop loss?
rows.answer: Morning, sir. The short dip trade has no stop because testing showed stops made it worse. With no stop and a 10-day exit, it earned about 6.5% and 2.4% a trade in the two test periods. With a tight stop it earned only about 0.5% and 0.4%. Dips usually wobble lower before they bounce, so a tight stop kicks you out right before the recovery.

rows.question: Can we buy today? Answer yes or no first, then why.
rows.answer: Morning, sir. Short answer: no, not really. The exposure dial still says OPEN, but only barely. Bitcoin closed at 80,888 against its 50-day average of 80,854, and the live price of about 80,170 is already under it. One daily close under that line shuts the dial, and cash becomes the position. Nothing is complete on any coin, and every coin's hourly trend is down. The trend portfolio is already out, holding cash. Want me to check what's close to firing?

Bitcoin closed at 80,888 against a 50-day average of 80,854, and the live price of about 80,170 is already under it. No Explorer setup is complete, and every coin is trending down on the 1-hour and 4-hour charts. One daily close under the 50-day shuts the dial, and my written view expects chop with a slight downward lean.

rows.answer: Morning, sir. My view is chop with a slight downward lean: Bitcoin is sitting on its 50-day average at about 80 thousand, and the live price of about 80,170 is now under it. The dial is still OPEN from yesterday's close, but one daily close under the 50-day shuts it, and breadth is weak: all 10 of our coins are down on the day and none are in a 1-hour uptrend.
